title: A fitted VAR(1) test supports long-period DOISST intervals but finds lower coverage for short-period OI v2
abstract: We tested uncertainty in SST artifact effects on radiative feedback. We used signed SST and five-model radiation-response aggregates. We fitted bivariate Gaussian VAR(1) noise to annual residuals. A nested test used 5,000 outer records and 1,000 paired block bootstrap draws per record. Nominal 95% intervals gave 94.84% coverage for the 1982-2022 DOISST correction effect and 95.24% for 1991-2011. Coverage was 93.44% for the 2001-2022 OI v2 correction effect and 92.90% for an added 2002-2022 window. The latter deficits exceed simulation counting error. A separate joint-trend region had much lower coverage before calibration. Its wide nonlinear projection did not directly measure scalar percentile coverage. The results support long-period DOISST intervals and identify moderate short-period undercoverage under the fitted noise model. Corrections and model responses remain fixed. Noise-model error, correction uncertainty and non-Gaussian climate variability limit the result. The package includes code, aggregate test results, source hashes and numerical checks.

display.caption: Paired percentile coverage in fitted-noise simulations and zero-denominator checks in 21-year windows.
Feedback changes from SST corrections. Scalar percentile intervals and conservative calibrated joint-region projections answer different uncertainty questions.
